correctness.rationale: Proof enumerates all candidate borders of a rotation with first and last symbols different: for cuts after a marker, the criterion is a>c; before a marker, a<c, using the three-one bound on numbers of markers in proper borders. Other cuts have a one-letter border. The binomial-composition double count handles periodic triples; rational moment formulas follow algebraically. Independent KMP comparison and direct prefix/suffix tests validated 27405 words through n=29; experiments are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

evidence: Harju--Nowotka proves every primitive binary word has at least two unbordered rotations and gives general upper bounds; these are consistent with our 2-or-3 statement but do not produce the strict three-gap criterion.

Holub--Müller characterizes words with exactly two unbordered conjugates by a recursive palindrome-related construction; the three-one two-equal subclass should be regarded as a specialized manifestation of that existing boundary, not a new general characterization of fully bordered words.
Clokie--Gabrić--Shallit gives all-word existence/maxima and unconditional expectation, not this conditioned distribution or exact indexed cut pattern.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Our claim does not assert novelty of the already known two-conjugate concept, unrestricted bounds, or the existence of three-conjugate words. Its contribution is an explicit exact full correlation in the first sparse case with a third unbordered shift, including all n class counts. Stronger all-weight results in sources were checked for whether they imply this data directly; none inspected provides the three-gap conditional law.

value.rationale: Border correlation is a central intrinsic invariant studied in the cited literature. Exactly three ones is the first fixed-marker binary stratum in which a third unbordered rotation appears: the theorem completely classifies all cut locations for infinitely many lengths, not merely a finite table or recomputation of an unrestricted maximum, and determines exact class sizes and sample moments. The result is an interpretable structural boundary of the fully bordered two-conjugate locus, with an explicit cyclic-necklace classification.
